correctness.rationale: For every distinct ordered pair, ordinary collision intensity is exactly \(2/(n-1)\). A simultaneous reset to distinct homes cannot collide, yielding an exact exponential law. Independent reset alarms add a nonnegative killing hazard \(r(1_{Y=A}+1_{X=B})\) and a strictly capturable configuration is reached with positive probability by any positive time, implying strict stochastic dominance via the forward survival equation. Symmetry reduces the killed generator to five classes (four when \(n=3\)); solving exact backward equations yields \((n-1)/2-(n-2)(n-1)^2r/[2Q_n(r)]\), and its derivative has sign of \(2(n-1)^2r^2-n(n+2)\). Standard-library rational check passed 3162 comparisons, including full unquotiented generators; separate symbolic matrix inversion and derivative factorization agreed identically. Infinite-domain validity rests on the exact generator algebra, not sampled cases.

originality.rationale: Full-text comparison establishes that prescribed-node encounter times with simultaneous discrete-time updates do not imply all-site first-collision absorption under asynchronous independent Poisson resets. Ohwa already proves the no-reset exponential complete-graph meeting law and is fully credited. The public odd-cycle first-collision Fourier theorem uses only shared geometric resets on a different graph. The new contribution is the strict all-deadline dominance combined with an exact positive gain, a unique optimized per-walker rate, and a nonzero large-graph efficiency limit. Search coverage is not a proof of priority, with possible unindexed broader results remaining.

value.rationale: Matching total reset alarm event budgets on a perfectly homogeneous network yields a strict all-time first-collision ranking even though common alarms are completely neutral. Exact rational mean and unique finite optimum quantify an experimentally interpretable reaction-upon-reset mechanism; the limiting saving of \(1/(4+2\sqrt2)\) is nonzero. This exact model sharpens the distinction between first collision anywhere and first encounter at a selected node, a motivated gap directly arising from 2025/2026 comparison literature, rather than a single parameter substitution or a known table recomputation.
